name: new_unchecked
declaration: const unsafe fn new_unchecked (pointer : Ptr) -> Pin < Ptr >
rules: Unless `Ptr::Target` implements `Unpin`, the caller must ensure that the data pointed to by `pointer` is not moved until it is dropped; for `Pin<&'a mut T>`, this obligation continues after `'a` ends or the `Pin` is dropped if the value has not yet been dropped.

Unless `Ptr::Target` implements `Unpin`, the caller must ensure that the storage of the data pointed to by `pointer` is not invalidated until the data is dropped; for `Pin<&'a mut T>`, this obligation continues after `'a` ends or the `Pin` is dropped if the value has not yet been dropped.
If `Ptr` implements `Deref`, the caller must ensure that its `Deref` implementation does not move out of its `self` argument and upholds the pinning invariants.
If `Ptr` implements `DerefMut`, the caller must ensure that its `DerefMut` implementation does not move out of its `self` argument and upholds the pinning invariants.
If `Ptr` implements `Drop`, the caller must ensure that its `Drop` implementation does not move out of its `self` argument.

Unless `Ptr::Target` implements `Unpin`, the caller must ensure that the value referenced by dereferencing `pointer` cannot subsequently be moved out, including by obtaining a `&mut Ptr::Target` and moving out through it.
When calling `Pin::new_unchecked(&mut var)` where `var` is a by-value closure capture, the caller must ensure that the closure itself is pinned.
When calling `Pin::new_unchecked(&mut var)` where `var` is a by-value closure capture, the caller must ensure that all uses of that capture respect its pinning.
When a closure is passed to another API, `Pin::new_unchecked` may be used on its captures only if that API explicitly documents that the closure is pinned.
